en: You've been told AI is why new grads are
ko: 갓 졸업한 사람들이 일자리를 못 구하는 건

en: struggling to find jobs.
A New York Fed study found the trouble
ko: 그런데 뉴욕 연준 연구에 따르면 문제는

en: started before ChatGPT existed.
The common version goes like this.
Companies adopted ChatGPT,
junior work got automated,
so the first rung of the career ladder disappeared.
ko: 그래서 경력 사다리의 첫 칸이 사라졌다는 거죠.

en: Videos telling that story have been
watched millions of times.
Young graduates are struggling.
That part is true.
The question is why,
because the answer changes what a graduate
should do about it.
In June 2026,
three economists published a study on the
New York Fed's research blog.
Their study looks at when the problem started,
and in which kinds of jobs.
Their answer points at a change that came
before AI tools were in wide use.
ko: AI 도구가 널리 쓰이기 전에 일어난 변화요.

en: A second study, from Stanford,
then adds a newer problem on top.
ko: 그 위에 더 새로운 문제를 얹습니다.

en: Start with the gap itself.
The New York Fed tracks recent college graduates,
aged 22 to 27.
In the second quarter of 2026,
their unemployment rate was about 5.6 percent.
And 42 percent of them were underemployed,
meaning they held a job that doesn't need a degree.
ko: 학위가 필요 없는 일을 하고 있었다는 뜻이에요.

en: For graduates under 29,
the unemployment rate averaged about 3.1
percent in the years before the pandemic.
In the years after,
it averaged about 3.7 percent,
a rise of roughly a fifth.
Over the same years,
older graduates went the other way.
Their rate edged down slightly.
On its own,
that pattern fits the AI explanation.
Juniors get replaced while seniors stay.
The researchers checked that.
They sorted jobs into two groups.
Jobs you can do from home,
like software engineering.
And jobs where you have to show up,
like mechanical engineering.
In the from-home jobs,
unemployment for young graduates rose by
about one percentage point between the
pre-pandemic years and 2022 to 2024.
Older workers in those same jobs saw a slight decline.
In the show-up jobs,
the gap between young and old widened
briefly in 2020,
then went back to where it had been.
So the gap opened in the jobs that went remote,
ko: 그러니까 격차는 원격으로 바뀐 일자리에서 벌어졌고,

en: and it didn't stay open in the jobs that
stayed in person.
By the study's count,
remote work has grown about four-fold
since the pandemic.
The timing points the same way.
Youth unemployment had been rising since the pandemic,
ko: 청년 실업은 팬데믹 때부터 오르고 있었고,

en: and ChatGPT only launched in November 2022.
Here is why distance seems to hurt new hires most.
ko: 거리가 왜 신입에게 특히 해로운지 보죠.

en: The researchers had internal data from one
ko: 연구진은 한 회사의 내부 데이터를 갖고 있었습니다.

en: Fortune 500 company.
When employees sat near each other,
they exchanged more feedback and more mentoring.
Even a short physical distance reduced that,
and it reduced it more for younger workers.
When that company's offices closed,
it hired fewer inexperienced workers.
In the authors' words,
a firm "shies away from employing
inexperienced workers if distance creates
barriers to training and development."
Two cautions apply.
The inside view comes from a single company,
ko: 내부 사정은 한 회사에서 나온 것이라,

en: so it can't stand in for the whole economy.
And the authors say remote work "can
explain" the rise.
That makes it an argument,
and the case is still open.
How much of the problem does remote work account for?
The researchers ran what they call a
back-of-the-envelope calculation. Their estimate:
remote work can explain about 64 percent
ko: 원격 근무가 약 64%를 설명할 수 있다.

en: of the recent increase in unemployment
among young college graduates.
So read it as a rough size.
They also tested an objection.
Maybe the from-home jobs are simply the
same jobs AI is good at.
ko: AI가 잘하는 일자리와 같은 게 아닐까?

en: So they held each occupation's AI exposure
fixed and ran the comparison again.
The gap between young and older workers
was still there.
That is the first problem.
A second study looks at the years after
ko: 두 번째 연구는 ChatGPT 이후의 몇 년을

en: ChatGPT and finds something else.
In August 2026,
Erik Brynjolfsson and two colleagues at
Stanford updated a study based on payroll
records from ADP.
ko: ADP 급여 기록을 바탕으로 한 연구죠.

en: They focused on workers aged 22 to 25 in
the occupations most exposed to AI.
ko: 그중에서도 AI 노출이 가장 큰 직업을 봤습니다.

en: By June 2026,
employment for those young workers was
about 19 percent lower,
relative to young workers in less exposed jobs.
ko: 노출이 적은 일자리의 젊은 층과 비교해서요.

en: In July 2025, the same gap was 15 percent.
The gap holds up when the authors control
for interest rates and for remote work.
Experienced workers in the same
occupations show no comparable gap.
The declines are concentrated in
occupations where AI tends to do the task
instead of the person.
Where AI is mainly used to help workers,
ko: AI가 주로 사람을 돕는 데 쓰이는 곳에선

en: young employment is flat or rising.
The Stanford authors attach their own cautions.
They call these descriptive patterns,
not causal estimates.
Some of the differences appear before
generative AI was widely used,
ko: 생성형 AI가 널리 쓰이기 전에도 보이고,

en: and the gap shrinks when education is
taken into account.
Their payroll sample also shows a bigger
gap than national surveys do.
ko: 전국 조사보다 격차를 크게 보여 줍니다.

en: There is a third suspect: interest rates.
In January 2022,
the Federal Reserve's benchmark rate was
close to zero,
at 0.08 percent.
By August 2023 it was 5.33 percent,
and it stayed there for about a year.
A working paper from the U.S.
Census Bureau looks at workers aged 22 to 24.
In the industries most exposed to AI,
their employment fell 12 percent in the
ten quarters after ChatGPT's release,
while less exposed industries held steady.
The paper then asks whether rising rates did that.
ko: 논문은 이어서 금리 인상 탓인지 묻습니다.

en: Its estimate is that up to a quarter of
the decline can be traced to the rate
hikes through 2023.
The paper finds rates can't account for
ko: 논문은 금리로는 설명이 안 된다고 봅니다.

en: the sharp hiring drop at the most AI-exposed firms.
ko: AI 노출이 가장 큰 기업들의 급격한 채용 감소는요.

en: The two studies cover overlapping years,
so this isn't a clean handoff from one
cause to the next.
They ask different questions.
The New York Fed study finds the early gap
ko: 뉴욕 연준 연구는 초기 격차를 찾습니다.

en: in jobs that went remote,
and it is still there when AI exposure is held fixed.
ko: AI 노출을 고정해도 그 격차는 남습니다.

en: The Stanford study finds a newer,
growing gap in jobs where AI does the task,
ko: 커지는 격차를 AI가 일을 하는 일자리에서 찾습니다.

en: and it is still there when remote work is
controlled for.
The simplest reading is that more than one
cause is stacking,
ko: 원인이 하나가 아니라 겹쳐 있다는 겁니다.

en: and the data can't yet say how much weight each carries.
ko: 각각의 비중은 데이터로 아직 알 수 없고요.

en: That still leaves a graduate with two
questions worth asking about any job.
ko: 어떤 일자리든 던져 볼 질문이 두 개 남습니다.

en: Will this role put me near people who can teach me?
ko: 이 자리는 나를 가르쳐 줄 사람 곁에 있게 해 주는가?

en: And is AI in this job doing the work,
ko: 그리고 이 일에서 AI는 일을 대신하는가,

en: or helping someone do it?
One problem is tied to remote work,
ko: 한 문제는 원격 근무와 연결돼 있고,

en: and its size rests on a rough estimate.
ko: 그 크기는 대략적인 추정에 기대고 있습니다.

en: The other is newer,
and it sits in jobs where AI does the task.
How much each one matters is still open.
ko: 각각이 얼마나 중요한지는 아직 열려 있습니다.

en: Which of those two questions applies to
ko: 이 두 질문 중 어느 쪽이

en: your own job search?
